build.reproducibility_note: GCC's default -frandom-seed is derived from the *source* file name: rebuilding src/player.cpp as base_head.cpp gives a different sha256 with identical code. Named player.cpp it reproduces the live artifact byte for byte.

alignment.why: -O3 fully inlines decide into moveDecision (nm shows no separate decide symbol), and the asm(.space 96) pad sits before moveDecision, so growth inside decide lands after the entry. Verified empirically with nm, not assumed: entry stayed at 0x1a50 for all three builds.

duty_none.reading: the always-paid 3 instructions are not measurable in cycles

ex_ante_estimate_vs_measurement.estimate: 3 always-paid instructions; about 15 in the taken block; 18-20 static; about 6 dynamic per call at a 20% duty cycle
ex_ante_estimate_vs_measurement.measured: 3.0000 always-paid (exact); about 24 in the taken block; +31 static; +16.568 dynamic per call
ex_ante_estimate_vs_measurement.verdict: the always-paid part was exactly right; the taken block was under-estimated by about 60% and the dynamic per-call total by 2.7x, because I did not budget for the second-order path divergence a changed anchor causes in code I did not touch.

cycles_priced.note: 0.2509 ns/cycle from the same-workload clock measurement

gold_price.gold_per_ns_source: the documented alignment result: buckets 0x20/0x30 cost +11.67 ns == about -128 gold/game
gold_price.which_and_why: the cycles number (-12.2) is the acceptance quantity and it sits between the two instruction prices, as it should: part of the delta is newly-retired instructions (marginal-priced) and part is a real branch and an extra 64-byte line touch at offset 1292 that the baseline never reads.

cost.harness: /tmp/xcycles.cpp: perf_event_open, exclude_kernel+exclude_hv, all three .so images loaded into one process, every rep measures every image back to back and the image order is rotated per rep so a within-window ramp cannot alias onto one variant.  Pinned with taskset. Reported statistic is the per-rep paired delta, so harness overhead and box drift cancel.

prior_art.diagnosed_root_cause_then: harvest precision: T-1's expedition extracts 4.81 gold/round (right region, right cell, shortest in and out) while ours was a blind lane sweep at 0.92-2.01 gold/round, about equal to its own central rate, i.e. no new money.
prior_art.negative_result_rule_7: cross-ring amount weighting judged negative: richness differences live in residence depth and the information layer, not the target-selection layer
prior_art.predecessor_construct: src/CHANGELOG.md, 8.9 'expedition organ v1-v3': a snapshot-triggered outer excursion with a STRICTER trigger than RICH (outer remaining>80, minus 40 per occupant to avoid crowds, timeout return, <70/>460 round curfew, two-segment lane machine).  All three variants judged income-neutral (T-1 pool 1069-1308 vs baseline 1266; Tundra pool 1141-1354 vs 1351).  v4 heap-memory raid also failed.
prior_art.relation_to_this_work: RICH is a CRUDER trigger than the retired v1-v3 (no threshold, no occupant avoidance, no timeout) and it reproduces the same judgement with a much tighter design: 240 holdout-split seeds, both order arms, a reversed-signal control and a byte-identical OFF.  This is an independent confirmation, not a new finding.

raid_differentiation.cannot_be_subtracted: different configuration, opponent, window and corpus; -477 and -52 are two separate measurements, never a difference
raid_differentiation.conclusion: the signal-triggered form IS demonstrably different from the scheduled raid -- the trigger is informative (arrival window mean 10.63 vs 4.87 static and 2.51 anti-signal) and the walk is shorter (median 3-4 rounds vs about 6) -- but the transit share, 0.849, is essentially the raid's 0.886, the median arrival gold is no better than standing still, and only 27.7% of excursions complete.  The difference is real and it is not enough.

excursion_arrival_rate.reading: 72-74% of excursions never arrive: the anchor is refreshed before the unit gets there

u1_pickup_per_game.reading: as the second mover the anti-informative POOR harvests the most: the gain is 'leave the contested centre', not 'find gold'

raid_differentiation.the_historical_negative: an outer-ring hotspot raid lost -477 gold/game paired; failure mode = walk about 6 rounds to a FIXED token-2 hotspot, arrive to a median of 0 gold, 88.6% of rounds in transit, only about 2 of 20 hotspot cells hold gold at any instant

gold_density_per_cell_by_region.reading: in the simulator the central 9x9 is the POOREST region per cell; gold_remaining is a raw total, not a density, and region 1 has 81 cells against 52 for each arm

signal_quality.source: /tmp/signal_decay.py over the first 40 games of /tmp/ac-o1 (baseline self-play, map1, costs 200,201), 3960 snapshot rounds
signal_quality.verdict: the sensor is genuinely informative and survives the travel delay in the MEAN (2.2x the static anchor, 2.1x POOR, 1.5x a random arm), but the MEDIAN is 2 against the static anchor's 2 and the zero rate is WORSE (43.6% vs 34.9%).  The advantage is entirely right-tail, and the target only persists 37% of the time, so the unit is redirected mid-flight.

simulator_bias.class_of_change: dispersion / scarcity -> systematically OVER-estimated by this simulator
simulator_bias.density_correction: under the same correction the centre's density becomes 0.269 x 1.444 = 0.388 per cell, which is HIGHER than every arm (0.302-0.354).  In the simulator the arms are 12-32% richer per cell; corrected, the centre is the richest.  The entire reward for leaving the centre that this experiment measures may not exist on the platform.
simulator_bias.direction_of_the_correction_on_my_number: both corrections push the verdict more negative: the positive second-mover-arm number is inflated, and the negative first-mover-arm number is understated in magnitude.  A negative verdict is therefore robust to the bias; a positive one would not have been.
simulator_bias.documented_central_under_supply: simulated central remaining 27 vs real 39 (sim/hunt_ab.py design note)

firing_rate_correction.method: /tmp/bias_rescale.py: rescale region 1's gold_remaining by 39/27 = 1.444 and recount the argmax

simulator_bias.npc_fidelity: the NPC model reproduces real NPC actions 38.7% of the time and is both too greedy and too centre-biased
simulator_bias.stock_vs_flow: not applicable to the income numbers: every delta is the engine's own final net_gold, never a sum of per-round ground values, so the 85-92% double-count hazard cannot enter.  These are contested-regime games (two strong players plus 7 NPCs), so no discount applies either.

verdict.does_the_retired_sensor_deserve_to_come_: no, not in this policy form
verdict.identified_value_of_the_information: rich minus poor is +35.51 +- 11.85 when we move first and -60.47 +- 10.29 when we move second, both significant on holdout with opposite signs.  Weighted at the measured live T-1 first-mover rate of 0.225 it is -38.88 +- 8.82 (95% CI -56.2 to -21.6): under the weighting that actually matters the information is worth NEGATIVE money.
verdict.one_line: the mechanism does not plausibly deliver a material part of +318 gold/game; on holdout it is worth at most +28 gold/game under the most favourable defensible weighting, and its own reversed-signal control beats it there by 4x
verdict.the_decisive_control: POOR, which steers at the region with the LEAST gold, gains MORE than RICH in the second-mover arm (+92.67 vs +32.20 on holdout) and loses more in the first-mover arm (-87.74 vs -52.23).  The gain is dispersion, not information.
what_would_have_to_change: the target persists only 37% of snapshots, so require two consecutive confirmations before re-anchoring

the advantage is right-tail only (mean 10.63, median 3), so gate on an absolute gold_remaining threshold instead of a bare argmax -- which is exactly what the retired 8.9 construct did, and it was still income-neutral
gold_remaining is a raw total over unequal areas (81 cells vs 52); a density signal would be a different and untested sensor
the excursion must be cheap: 0.849 transit share is the whole loss, so the destination must be reachable in 1-2 rounds, which the arm centroids at Manhattan 9-12 are not
verdict.why_not_undecidable: the sample is decisive rather than ambiguous: OFF is exactly 0.00 on 240/240 seeds, every arm-level effect is 3-12 sigma, in-sample and holdout agree in sign on all four arm statistics, and the reversed-signal control is LARGER in magnitude than the candidate in both arms.
